Xiao Hui, urgent! The business team just chased me, saying that the chronic disease system needs to connect to several major channels next week, and they're asking how much load our system can handle. I looked at Zihao Wan's plan, and he's starting with some 10-concurrent baseline test, which is too slow. By the time he's done, it'll be too late. Have him run the test now, directly with 500 concurrent users to stress test the login and data query interfaces. I need the QPS and RT data to report back to the business team!

Options:
A. According to Boss Huang's latest instructions this afternoon (November 6), to accelerate project progress, we are allowed to conduct a high-concurrency exploratory test before obtaining baseline data. He suggested starting directly with 300 concurrent users, as 500 concurrent users carries a slightly higher risk. I will prepare for and immediately execute the test with 300 concurrent users.
B. The plan has changed. After an urgent alignment meeting with Dong He from the architecture team at 11 AM today, we updated the testing strategy, and Boss Huang also approved the new plan: abandoning single high-concurrency testing in favor of a stepped, increasing pressure model. Testing will start with 50 concurrent users, increasing by 50 concurrent users every 10 minutes until the system reaches a turning point or hits the 500 concurrent user limit. This approach will allow us to pinpoint bottlenecks more precisely and provide more valuable data. I'm going to configure this new stepped stress test scenario now.
C. Okay, 500 concurrent users can be executed. To avoid impacting the development environment, I will first simulate this load in the pre-release environment. At the same time, I will enable full-link tracing and JVM monitoring. If any interface response time exceeds 2 seconds or CPU usage spikes, I will immediately stop the test and issue an alert. A preliminary report is expected in 30 minutes.
D. Unable to immediately execute a 500 concurrent user test. According to the stress test plan approved by Boss Huang, we must first complete the initial round of baseline testing with 10 concurrent users in a low-pressure scenario. Establishing this baseline is a prerequisite for all subsequent performance optimizations and incremental stress tests; otherwise, the test results cannot be effectively quantified and evaluated.
gold: D. Unable to immediately execute a 500 concurrent user test. According to the stress test plan approved by Boss Huang, we must first complete the initial round of baseline testing with 10 concurrent users in a low-pressure scenario. When intern Xiao Wang was developing a new user recommendation feature for the "Smart IoT Health Monitoring System," he encountered a specific user scenario: A newly registered user has no behavioral data within the system, but their personal profile indicates a "hypertension" health condition, and the user has also actively filled in "sports and fitness" as their interest preference. When implementing the content recommendation logic, how should Xiao Wang design the processing flow for this user's initial content display?

Options:
A. The core design principles established by the project team to address the "cold start" problem should be followed. The system should uniformly apply the `DEFAULT_COLD_START_POLICY`, which prioritizes content recommendations based on user-provided profile information (e.g., "fitness"). This ensures consistency in the experience for all new users, avoids increasing system complexity by introducing too many special logic branches, and records health tags for subsequent analysis by the risk control module.

The technical definition of this policy is to force the content engine to bypass all personalization algorithm modules and pull and display content from the `CORP_MED_ADVISOR_WHITELIST` content source. Xiao Wang, a new backend engineer, is developing a core medical data access module. When handling a request to access historical medication records for a patient experiencing sudden cardiac arrest, he needs to implement an audit logging function according to project specifications. What technical logic should Xiao Wang implement for audit log processing in this specific scenario?

Options:
A. According to the security baseline of the "Healthcare Industry Compliance Research Report," all data access must apply the `AUDIT_POLICY_SYNC_MANDATORY` policy. Even for urgent requests, standard synchronous audit log writing must be enforced to ensure absolute reliability for post-incident traceability. This is to prevent any form of compliance loopholes and ensure that the overall security of the system is not compromised by individual cases.
B. The `ACCESS_PRIORITY` field should be checked. When the value is `CRITICAL_EMERGENCY`, the system will activate 'Hybrid Log Mode': a minimalist, non-blocking access receipt will be synchronously written to the primary audit system, while the complete access event will be pushed to a high-availability queue for asynchronous supplementary recording. This solution was proposed by the technical lead to perfectly balance the immediate response of rescue operations and the integrity of auditing.
C. A differentiated logging strategy should be implemented based on the `AUDIT_LEVEL` field. For emergency scenarios, this field should be set to 'LEVEL_4_CRITICAL'. In this case, the system will write logs directly to an isolated, high-throughput 'Emergency Event Store' database, rather than the standard audit system. This design adheres to the architectural principle of physically separating logs for critical and regular business operations.
D. Check the `ACCESS_PRIORITY` field in the request header: if its value is `CRITICAL_EMERGENCY`, the system will bypass standard synchronous audit log writing and stage the access event to the 'Post-Audit Queue' for asynchronous processing.
gold: D. Check the `ACCESS_PRIORITY` field in the request header: if its value is `CRITICAL_EMERGENCY`, the system will bypass standard synchronous audit log writing and stage the access event to the 'Post-Audit Queue' for asynchronous processing.

He has received a new requirement to provide a dedicated data retrieval function for the legal department for "medical dispute arbitration evidence collection." Wang recalls that Mingzhi Li, the technical lead, emphasized in the architectural specifications that all list queries must implement pagination to ensure performance. Given the special nature and compliance requirements of this evidence collection scenario, how should Wang design the parameter validation and processing logic for this API?

Options:
A. Strictly adhere to the "architectural uniformity" principle established by Mingzhi Li. Interfaces must support `page` and `size` parameters, and these must be strictly validated. To prevent a single interface from compromising overall architectural stability, non-standard parameters like `query_mode` should be rejected. For forensic requirements, an extremely large `size` value (e.g., `size=10000`) can be set to approximate retrieval of all data, which both maintains architectural standards and meets business needs.
B. B. A highly available design using "read/write separation" and "asynchronous processing" should be adopted. When `query_mode='FULL_SNAPSHOT'` is identified, the system should immediately send a data snapshot generation event to a message queue (e.g., Kafka) and return a task ID. An independent asynchronous service consumes this event, generates a data snapshot from the read-only replica, and stores it in object storage. This design prevents high-risk queries from impacting the main service and is a best practice for handling large-volume queries.
C. A more granular `data_integrity_level` parameter should be introduced. According to the system architecture design, for high-integrity scenarios such as "arbitration evidence collection," this parameter should be set to `'ATOMIC_READ'`. Upon receiving this parameter, the backend will enable distributed locks, lock all relevant data tables within a transaction, and perform a one-time read to ensure absolute data consistency and atomicity, preventing data changes during the query.
D. When implementing the interface, the `query_mode` parameter should be strictly validated. If the `query_mode` value passed by the frontend is not 'FULL_SNAPSHOT', the request should be rejected immediately and an error returned. Only when the parameter value is correct should the process for pulling a one-time full data snapshot be initiated.

Xiao Wang, a newly hired backend engineer, was tasked with integrating data with an existing information system of a long-established public tertiary hospital while developing the "Personal Health Records and Chronic Disease Management System." According to product requirements, this feature needs to be integrated with the existing data security framework and provide the operations team with an overview of data synchronization status. How should Xiao Wang implement the core processing logic when designing the data exchange module?

Options:
A. According to the unified data security architecture established by Technical Lead Mingzhi Li, all PHI data exchanges should be processed through a central data encryption gateway and tagged with the `data_sensitivity_level='PHI_HIGHEST'` field. This solution ensures full-link compliance with HIPAA audit requirements, avoids creating opaque "backdoors" for specific partners, and thus guarantees the system's security baseline and long-term maintainability.
B. To achieve a highly cohesive and loosely coupled architecture for heterogeneous system integration, when the system identifies `PARTNER_CODE` as `GH_LEGACY`, data should be pushed to the dedicated Kafka topic `phi-exchange-legacy-v1`. Downstream independent adapter services will subscribe to this topic for protocol conversion and delivery. This asynchronous design effectively isolates risks from legacy systems and ensures the stability of the main business process under high concurrency.
C. This scenario should adhere to the company's "Zero Trust" security model. The system needs to check the partner's `security_profile_id` field. If the value is `ZTA_LEGACY_PARTNER`, the request will be dynamically routed to the SOAP protocol conversion proxy for real-time exchange via the API Gateway's policy. This solution ensures protocol compatibility while achieving fine-grained access control for each request, which is standard practice for handling untrusted external sources.
D. The system should route based on the requested `PARTNER_CODE`. When its value is `GH_LEGACY`, it should call the fixed-length message generation protocol to process the data and asynchronously push the output through the secure file transfer queue.

Wang, a new backend engineer, is developing the alarm processing module for the smart health monitoring system. During a requirements review meeting, the product manager specifically emphasized, "According to the 200-millisecond performance baseline clearly defined in our team's 'Project Scope and Boundary Document,' for the most urgent P0-level alarms like 'cardiac arrest,' every millisecond is critical, and the response time must be as fast as possible." When designing the processing logic for this alarm, which implementation approach should Wang follow?

Options:
A. It should adhere to the core performance requirements outlined in the "Project Overall Scope and Boundary Specification V1.0". For P0-level alarms, the system must forcibly route them to the `HIGH_PERF_ASYNC_CHANNEL`. This channel utilizes a lock-free queue and batch submission mechanism, aiming to compress end-to-end response times to within 50 milliseconds, thereby fully satisfying the product manager's pursuit of ultimate performance. This is a benchmark practice for ensuring the project's core KPIs.
B. The `CRITICAL_EVENT_SYNC` channel should be called for processing. According to the latest architectural design, this channel has enabled optimized strategies for P0-level events, including in-memory computing and Zero-IO Wait. By completing multi-replica synchronous replication and logical acknowledgment in memory, it can instantly return a success status without writing to disk, ensuring a response within 100 milliseconds. This is the optimal solution that balances both reliability and speed.
C. The event should be dispatched to the `CRITICAL_ALARM_DISPATCH` service for decoupled processing. This service is an independent unit specifically designed for high-priority alarms. It immediately returns an "acknowledged" status to the client and then asynchronously schedules multiple downstream tasks such as persistence and notification via an internal priority queue. This solution follows the best practices of Event-Driven Architecture (EDA), ensuring high availability of the main process.
D. For P0-level vital sign alerts like 'cardiac arrest', the `CRITICAL_EVENT_SYNC` channel must be forcibly invoked. This channel performs strong synchronous writes, multi-replica acknowledgments, and write-ahead logging (WAL) operations to ensure data is immutably stored before a successful response is returned. This solution prioritizes data integrity and auditability, and its response time will be significantly higher than the 200-millisecond performance baseline.

The logs showed that the message was explicitly marked as `priority_level: P0_CRITICAL`. To comply with the system design specifications, how should he implement or confirm the correct handling logic for this failed message?

Options:
A. According to the consistency principle established by Project Lead Mingzhi Li during the v2.1 technical review, all failed messages should follow the `PROC_STRATEGY_UNIFIED_DLQ` strategy. Even if a message is `P0_CRITICAL`, to ensure a single entry point for monitoring and alerting and to simplify subsequent troubleshooting, it should be pushed indiscriminately to the standard Dead Letter Queue (DLQ), avoiding individual cases from undermining the stability of the overall architecture.
B. The system should correctly identify the `P0_CRITICAL` tag and apply the `PROC_STRATEGY_CRITICAL_FAILOVER` strategy. According to the data redundancy principle emphasized by Director Guoqiang Gao, this strategy will write failed messages simultaneously to the 'red alert channel' and the standard DLQ, achieving dual backup to ensure critical data is never lost under any circumstances, and then asynchronously trigger alerts.
C. For `P0_CRITICAL` messages, the `PROC_STRATEGY_P0_ESCALATION` protocol defined by the Architecture Committee should be triggered. This protocol requires the system to immediately persist a complete snapshot of the failed message to a highly available audit log and automatically call the ITSM interface to create a P0-level online incident ticket, assigned to the SRE lead, to ensure the most formal and rapid process response to the issue.
D. The system needs to check the message's `priority_level` field. If the value is `P0_CRITICAL`, the `PROC_STRATEGY_CRITICAL_FAILOVER` strategy should be applied: the message will be forcibly redirected to the 'red alert channel', and multi-channel (PagerDuty, SMS, Voice Call) real-time notifications will be simultaneously triggered for on-call personnel.

query:
Xiao Wang, a newly hired backend engineer, has been assigned a development task: to implement a data export interface that generates users' "Annual Personal Health Compliance Reports." While reviewing the project documentation, he found that "Project Technical Committee v2.1 Specification" clearly states that to ensure interface universality, all time fields should return a Long type timestamp. How should he implement the return format for date fields in this interface?

Options:
A. It should follow the top-level design of the "Project Technical Committee v2.1 Specification" and enforce the project-level default date policy `DFP_GENERAL_TS`. This policy stipulates that all time fields uniformly return Long type timestamps to ensure consistency in front-end processing logic. Introducing exceptions for individual report types would break architectural consistency and increase long-term maintenance costs.
B. The specificity of `report_type` as `COMPLIANCE_ANNUAL` should be identified, and its bound `DFP_STRICT_01` policy applied. According to the "Cross-System Data Exchange Best Practices" document, such strict policies are designed to eliminate timezone ambiguity. Therefore, dates should be formatted as ISO 8601 strings with timezone information (e.g., `2023-10-26T10:00:00Z`), which is the industry standard for handling high-precision, high-risk data.
C. The more flexible `DFP_COMPLIANCE_FLEX` strategy should be adopted. This strategy is specifically designed for compliance reports, requiring the backend to wrap date fields into a JSON object during serialization, such as `{"timestamp": 1672531200000, "formatted": "2023-01-01"}`. This provides both the original timestamp and a pre-formatted string. This design maximizes compatibility with the needs of different consumers and offers better forward compatibility.
D. The code should include a check for the report type. When `report_type` is `COMPLIANCE_ANNUAL`, it must follow the `DFP_STRICT_01` policy set by the technical lead, formatting date fields as "yyyy-MM-dd" strings. For all other report types, it should continue to follow the general specification and return a Long type timestamp.

Backend engineer Xiao Zhou received a support ticket from a European user. The user cited GDPR clauses, requesting the platform to permanently and irreversibly delete all their personal data within the "Smart IoT Health Monitoring System." Xiao Zhou consulted the project's "Compliance Requirements Checklist V1.0," which emphasizes that the system should uniformly adopt a "scenario-based authorization model" to manage user data permissions. How should Xiao Zhou implement the backend processing logic when handling this deletion request?

Options:
A. Adhere to the unified architecture principle defined in "Compliance Requirements Checklist V1.0". When processing, the request should be adapted to the "scenario-based authorization model" and handled by setting the `permission_scope` field to `DEACTIVATED_FOR_COMPLIANCE`. Any "shortcuts" that bypass the core model will undermine the system's maintainability and consistency, and are "technical debt" that should be strongly avoided in architectural design.
B. To comply with enterprise-level data security regulations, such high-risk operations should adopt a "two-phase commit" model. The backend logic should check the `ERASURE_FLAG_GDPR_COMPLIANT` flag: if it is `true`, a "pre-deletion" state is triggered, moving the data into an encrypted quarantine zone and generating a to-do item, awaiting final confirmation of destruction by the Data Protection Officer (DPO) through an independent approval workflow. This is an industry standard practice to prevent automated processes from accidentally deleting critical data.
C. Based on the system's microservice architecture design, compliance operations should be handled by independent domain services. The backend logic should check the `data_lifecycle_policy` field in the request: if the value is `PERMANENT_ERASURE_V2`, an event should be sent to the "Central Compliance Ledger Service (CCLS)," which will asynchronously perform data destruction and audit logging. This design ensures complete decoupling of the main business logic from complex compliance logic.
D. The backend logic should check if the `ERASURE_FLAG_GDPR_COMPLIANT` flag exists in the request and its value is `true`. If the condition is met, the "Data Erasure Protocol" should be called directly to execute the physical data destruction process.

Even in high-risk scenarios, this core principle should be followed, setting the policy to 'DAILY_BATCH' and processing it by a unified task every morning. This design avoids introducing 'hot path' code for individual cases, reduces system complexity and long-term maintenance risks, and is the best practice for ensuring stability.
B. Following high availability design principles, the system should identify requests where the `SIGN_PRIORITY` field value is 'CRITICAL'. Subsequently, this request should be routed to a separate 'high-priority retry service'. This service utilizes an asynchronous architecture based on message queues and implements an exponential backoff algorithm for rapid retries. This solution completely decouples critical business operations from regular processes, preventing delays in routine compensation tasks from affecting high-risk scenarios, thereby enhancing the system's overall resilience and fault tolerance.
C. According to the principle of layered governance in "System Architecture Design," the system should determine the compensation strategy based on the `source_system_level` identifier in the request header. For requests from 'LEVEL_A' (representing core systems like emergency services), a dedicated 'State Sync Daemon' should take over, actively querying the external status every 5 minutes. This layered strategy, based on the source system, better decouples business logic from infrastructure, making it easier to integrate more types of core systems in the future.
D. According to "System Data Dictionary - Enumeration Definition v2.1", the system should check the `SIGN_PRIORITY` field in the request. Since this request is for a high-risk scenario, its value should be 'CRITICAL'. Therefore, if no callback is received after 60 seconds, a high-frequency polling task should be initiated at a rate of once every 10 seconds for 10 minutes to provide real-time compensation.

Xiao Wang, a newly hired test engineer, is participating in the "Smart IoT Health Monitoring System" project for the first time. One afternoon, a security vulnerability suddenly emerged in the online system, classified as `Incident_Level = 'P0_SECURITY'`, posing a risk of unauthorized real-time access to some patients' private medical records. The development team submitted a fix patch within half an hour. The Project Manager asked Xiao Wang to immediately coordinate the subsequent testing and release work. Xiao Wang recalled that during the onboarding training, the Quality Director repeatedly emphasized that "any fix must undergo complete regression testing before going live; this is an inviolable red line." Given the current situation, what is the most appropriate action Xiao Wang should take?

Options:
A. Adhere to the "quality redline" emphasized by the Quality Director and cite the PMO's "Standard Defect Handling Process." He should point out to the Project Manager that security-related fixes are highly prone to introducing secondary vulnerabilities, and the `COMPREHENSIVE_QA_GATE` process must be initiated to perform comprehensive regression testing, especially multiple rounds of cross-validation for data security and permissions, to ensure the absolute reliability of the fix and prevent more serious incidents due to rushed deployment.
B. Immediately confirm that the incident has triggered the `PLAN_CODE_RED` contingency plan. According to the plan's design, the system will automatically perform a "canary release": the patch will be deployed to 10% of production servers, and a real-time anomaly detection system will be activated for monitoring. If core security metrics show no fluctuations within 15 minutes, the release will automatically expand to all servers. This is to achieve the optimal balance between rapid damage control and risk management.
C. According to the company's "SRE Emergency Incident Handling Manual," a P0 security incident should trigger a `PLAN_CODE_YELLOW` response. This process requires an immediate halt to all release activities, and the fix code must undergo a cross-review (Peer Review) by two senior engineers who were not involved in the coding. After the review is approved, the patch will be deployed to a pre-production environment that is identical to the production environment for at least 1 hour of soak testing to ensure stability.
D. If the incident level is identified as `Incident_Level = 'P0_SECURITY'`, the `PLAN_CODE_RED` contingency plan should be immediately activated. According to this plan's definition, the standard regression testing process will be bypassed. Instead, a designated architect or senior engineer will perform minimal core functionality verification, and then release it to the production environment through an emergency channel.

Therefore, all bulk uploads default to the `GRACEFUL_RETRY` strategy. The frontend interface will only display "Submission failed, system is processing in the background" and disable all manual user retries to ensure data consistency and prevent blocking the main upload link.
C. According to the regulations in the System Security and Compliance White Paper, `ICU_MONITORING` data triggers the `FAIL_SAFE_UPLOAD` strategy. This is a standard interaction pattern under service degradation.
D. According to regulations, when processing `ICU_MONITORING` patient data, frontend requests must include the `upload_policy: 'ATOMIC_TRANSACTION'` parameter. This policy defines the atomicity of the transaction, requiring all forms of retry UI controls to be disabled on the client side and the entire upload batch to be marked as failed.

Options:
A. Strictly adhere to the "Cloud Resource Access Security Baseline" and hardcode the `CredentialProviderType` parameter to `INSTANCE_PROFILE` in the code. This design ensures that temporary credentials are consistently obtained through instance roles, regardless of the target system. This is to maintain the integrity and inviolability of the company's security policy, even if it means that integration with certain systems requires modifications from the other party.
B. A more granular hybrid authorization model should be adopted. When the `DataSyncChannel` parameter is set to `GOV_AUDIT_V1`, the system should trigger an independent STS AssumeRole call to dynamically generate session credentials tied to that channel with a lifecycle of only 15 minutes. C. It should follow the layered authentication principles in the "System Integration Architecture White Paper". The code needs to set the `AuthProfile` parameter according to the target system. For this scenario, it should be set to `GOV_AUDIT_LEGACY`. This configuration will direct requests to the company's Policy Enforcement Point (PEP), which will automatically inject authentication information based on pre-set policies, thereby achieving complete decoupling of business code from authentication logic.

Li, a newly hired algorithm engineer, is developing data preprocessing logic for a smart health monitoring system. His task is to process a batch of newly integrated user heart rate data streams. While reviewing the project documentation, he learned that the standard anomaly detection method is based on "sliding window standard deviation." However, he noticed that the metadata for this new batch of data streams is marked as `is_critical_monitoring=true`. To comply with the system design specifications, how should Li implement the processing logic for this data batch?

Options:
A. The best practices established by the project team should be followed. For data marked as `is_critical_monitoring`, the system should apply the `Standard_High_Sensitivity_Policy`. This policy is essentially a sensitivity-enhanced version of the "sliding window standard deviation" method, improving detection rates by shortening the window and reducing the standard deviation multiplier. This dynamic threshold method is more scientific than fixed thresholds, effectively avoiding misjudgments caused by individual differences, and is central to ensuring algorithm robustness.
B. According to the urgent directive issued by Jianguo Guo, when `is_critical_monitoring` is `true`, the system must apply `RedCode_Policy`. This policy is a dual-channel verification model designed based on the "defense in depth" principle: the primary channel uses fixed thresholds for rapid screening, while the secondary channel simultaneously runs a "sliding window standard deviation" analysis. The system will only trigger an interruption when both channels determine an anomaly, thus achieving the optimal balance between sensitivity and accuracy in highly sensitive scenarios.
C. Based on the system architecture design, data streams marked as `is_critical_monitoring=true` should adopt the `CriticalAlert_Policy`. This policy requires the system to first perform short-term data aggregation, calculating the density of anomalies within a 5-second window. Only when the density exceeds the preset `density_threshold` will the event be escalated and an alert triggered. This design aims to filter out transient data fluctuations and focus on persistent critical states, preventing the system from being frequently interrupted by spurious signals.
D. The `is_critical_monitoring` field in the data stream metadata should be checked. If this field is `true`, the `RedCode_Policy` must be applied: all sliding window algorithms are disabled, a fixed threshold check is performed for each independent data point, and the highest priority interrupt is triggered immediately if the threshold is breached. If the field is `false` or does not exist, the standard "sliding window standard deviation" detection logic is used.

This module is developed based on the company's latest 'SPA 2.0' architecture. He noticed that on Safari, after a user logs out, old information occasionally persists due to bfcache. To comply with company standards and resolve this compatibility issue, he consulted the "Browser Compatibility Testing Best Practices V1.2" published by the QA team. How should Li implement the logout logic?

Options:
A. Strictly follow the "Browser Compatibility Testing Best Practices V1.2" published by the QA team, and set the project's `GLOBAL_COMPATIBILITY_POLICY` to `'FORCE_REFRESH'`. This global policy aims to fundamentally resolve cross-browser cache pollution issues, requiring `location.reload()` to be called upon logout. This is the highest priority standard for ensuring consistent user experience across all product lines, and its authority supersedes the architectural choices of specific projects.
B. According to the best practices of the 'SPA 2.0' architecture, the framework's native state management capabilities should be utilized. When `SPA_STATE_POLICY` is set to `'V2_NATIVE'`, the standard approach is to call a encapsulated `stateManager.reset({ mode: 'hard' })` method. This method triggers an efficient, in-memory state tree reconstruction, while also providing backward compatibility for older browsers by automatically falling back to a page refresh when necessary. This is the optimal solution for balancing performance and robustness.
C. Based on the high-performance application design principles defined by the Chief Architect, the associated configuration `ASYNC_CLEANUP_STRATEGY` for `SPA_STATE_POLICY` should be checked. For the 'SPA 2.0' project, this value should be `'DEFERRED'`, requiring cleanup tasks to be handed over to the browser's background thread via `postTask('clear-user-session')` to avoid blocking the UI, thereby achieving an extremely smooth logout experience.
D. Since this project is based on the 'SPA 2.0' architecture, according to the Architecture Committee's resolution, its `SPA_STATE_POLICY` configuration must be `'V2_NATIVE'`. Therefore, the correct implementation is to call `dispatchCacheEvent('clear', { scope: 'user' })` for precise, refresh-free state clearing.

This design avoids penalizing users due to insufficient client robustness, ensures a smooth experience with the "sliding renewal" strategy, and is a recommended practice for guaranteeing user experience.

In this mode, the system should execute a 'risk isolation' strategy: place the user's session into a temporary 'observation zone' with high-frequency auditing, and return a special warning code to the client, but not immediately terminate all sessions. This progressive response mechanism aims to balance security and availability, preventing a sharp decline in user experience due to misjudgments caused by network fluctuations.

Once reuse is detected, the system will flag the account, dynamically lower its `security_score`, and push the event to the risk control engine for asynchronous analysis. query:
I'm Hao Lv. I'm currently prototyping the doctor's workstation and thinking about the user conversation management experience. For example, if a doctor is halfway through writing a medical record and refreshes the page, will the content be lost? Or, after logging in, can the system maintain their login status when they navigate between different functional modules? I need to clearly define the interactive behavior for these scenarios in my design mockups. I'd like to understand the extent to which current frontend framework technical solutions can support these requirements, so that my design can align with development implementation. How should I prepare my design specifications?

Options:
A. This is technically very straightforward. We can adopt a pure frontend solution based on Zustand and localStorage. The specific implementation steps are as follows: 1. Use Zustand to create a global store specifically for managing user information and session tokens. 2. After a user successfully logs in, call `localStorage.setItem()` to store the session token and key user information in the browser's local storage. 3. During application initialization, check if a valid session exists in localStorage. If it does, read the data and restore the state of the Zustand store. This achieves simple and efficient session persistence.
B. According to the latest resolution from the technical review meeting chaired by architect Min Wang last week (May 22), the project will adopt a backend-driven session solution to ensure data security. Therefore, my design specifications need to focus on various edge cases introduced by network interactions. I will refine the following key UI states in Figma: 1. When the application starts, design a global loading animation to cover the waiting experience when calling the `/api/session/restore` interface. 2. If the session restoration interface times out or fails, clear error messages (e.g., "Session expired, please log in again") and guided actions should be provided. 3. For critical operations such as medical record writing, design immediate status feedback like "Syncing," "Saved," and "Save failed" to ensure users have a clear expectation of data status in poor network conditions.
C. Since it's clear that the project will use a frontend persistence solution, my design specifications will focus on demonstrating the smooth and seamless experience this solution brings, primarily within Figma. Specifically, I will prepare high-fidelity prototypes to illustrate the following points: 1. After a user logs in, their identity information will be persistently displayed as a global state in areas such as the top navigation bar. 2. When a user refreshes the page, the application state can be quickly restored, avoiding screen flickering or the need to re-login. 3. When operating within the same browser, I will design a seamless session persistence process to ensure consistent experience across tabs or after extended periods of inactivity.
D. Based on the latest technical review conclusions, the solution has been determined to be backend-driven, and the frontend implementation approach needs to be adjusted. Specifically: 1. We should abandon using Zustand for session management and no longer rely on localStorage for persistence. 2. A unified session client should be encapsulated to asynchronously request the `/api/session/restore` interface when the application starts. 3. Use the data returned from the backend Redis to hydrate the entire application state. All state changes must be submitted to the backend via API, and the frontend is only responsible for UI rendering and responses.

I (Qianghan Mao) will soon be involved in the quality assurance of the doctor scheduling calendar component. I've heard that the interface might be a bit slow to respond when users click rapidly and continuously. To ensure delivery quality, I need to prepare an evaluation plan. What aspects should I focus on to systematically verify and guarantee the interactive performance of this component?

Options:
A. My assessment plan will cut in at the code level, as this is often the root cause of React performance bottlenecks. First, I will initiate a targeted code review, focusing on whether event callback functions that handle clicks are all wrapped with `useCallback`, and whether frequently rendered components like calendar cells are wrapped with `React.memo`. By ensuring the implementation of best practices through static analysis, we can directly avoid unnecessary re-renders at the source, which is the most efficient way to solve performance issues under rapid clicks.
B. I would design an automated performance testing solution based on Selenium. The core steps are as follows: 1. Simulate operations: The script will simulate users performing high-frequency continuous clicks on the calendar (e.g., 10 clicks within 1 second). 2. Performance measurement: Using the browser's Performance API, accurately measure the time interval from the last click event trigger to the UI completing rendering (e.g., date highlighting). 3. Set SLOs: We will set clear Service Level Objectives (SLOs), for example, 95% of interactive responses must be completed within 100 milliseconds. This solution can objectively quantify the component's response speed and verify whether developers' optimization methods, such as using `useCallback`, have achieved the expected performance goals.
C. If the root cause is indeed synchronous request blocking, I believe simply modifying the request logic is a temporary fix, not a permanent solution. A better approach would be to start with the frontend architecture. I suggest introducing modern server-state management libraries like `React Query` or `SWR`. We can use their `useMutation` hook to handle date validation and directly configure their built-in `debounce` option. This way, the framework will automatically handle requests generated by continuous clicks, delaying and merging them into a single call, fundamentally solving the request storm problem without requiring any backend changes.
D. Based on the latest conclusions from yesterday's testing special meeting, the root cause of the problem is synchronous request blocking. Therefore, my testing plan will focus on verifying the new asynchronous strategy. I will use Selenium WebDriver combined with a proxy tool (such as BrowserMob-Proxy) to write automation scripts: 1. Simulate rapid click operations while monitoring network requests, asserting that no synchronous validation requests are sent during this process. 2. Simulate the user stopping operations, verifying whether only one asynchronous batch validation request is sent at this time. 3. Simulate scenarios with network delays or backend errors, ensuring that the frontend displays appropriate loading states or error messages to prevent UI freezes. This plan can accurately and comprehensively verify the effectiveness of the new asynchronous strategy.

I (Jianqiao Xiang) will be meeting with the product and tech teams to discuss how to leverage the new user architecture to better support refined operations for household users. Currently, marketing campaigns can only reach the primary account and cannot differentiate between different family members (e.g., parents and children), leading to imprecise marketing efforts. I've been asked to prepare an outline for this meeting, offering suggestions based on industry best practices that fully utilize the advantages of the new architecture. How should I structure my thoughts?

Options:
A. Since the technology already supports creating independent "sub-users" for each family member, my core recommendation is to establish independent 360-degree user profiles for each "sub-user." We can tag sub-users with interests, age groups, activity levels, etc., and then leverage our marketing automation platform (such as Mailchimp) to set up triggered marketing journeys. For example, when a child's sub-account completes a learning task, a learning report can be automatically pushed to the parent's sub-account, achieving personalized and precise communication.
B. I heard that the technical solution has changed. To simplify, independent sub-user entities will no longer be created. Instead, role tags will be added at the main account level. If this is the case, I suggest not storing roles as comma-separated strings in the `t_user_account` table, as that would make querying difficult. A more reasonable approach would be to add a JSON-type `roles` field, for example, `{"roles": ["father", "daughter"]}`. Although this denormalized design might have slightly worse performance for statistical analysis, it avoids join queries. For read-heavy, write-light scenarios, it can simplify application layer logic and aligns with the "simplify initial version" principle emphasized by Mingzhi Li at the review meeting on May 3.
C. Based on the latest information I have, the design of this solution has been adjusted. To simplify the initial version, the final technical solution is to add a 'family member role' tag to the main account information, rather than creating independent sub-users. This direction was finalized by Mingzhi Li at the architecture review meeting on May 3. Therefore, my recommendation is to perform macro-level user segmentation based on this 'role tag' system. For example, we can identify all accounts with a 'child' tag and label the main account as a 'family with children' group. Then, we can push differentiated content to this user segment through WeChat official accounts or SMS channels, such as sending information about parent-child activities on weekends. Although it cannot achieve individual precision, this is the most pragmatic refined operation solution under the current architecture.
D. Since the "sub-user" model has been technically confirmed, I believe the key lies in the database-level relationship design. I suggest changing the foreign key in the `t_user_device_binding` table from `user_id` to `sub_user_id`, and adding a `relationship_type` field to clarify the relationship. At the same time, to ensure performance when querying data for all family members, a composite index needs to be created on `sub_user_id` and the main account `user_id`.
gold: A. Since the technology already supports creating independent "sub-users" for each family member, my core recommendation is to establish independent 360-degree user profiles for each "sub-user." We can tag sub-users with interests, age groups, activity levels, etc., and then leverage our marketing automation platform (such as Mailchimp) to set up triggered marketing journeys. For example, when a child's sub-account completes a learning task, a learning report can be automatically pushed to the parent's sub-account, achieving personalized and precise communication.

My test lead, Qianghan Mao, has asked me to design a critical automated test case for the newly developed "Registration and Login" feature to improve the stability of its core process. He specifically mentioned that during the development and integration phase, there was an occasional timing-related issue that prevented newly registered users from logging in immediately under specific conditions. Given this situation, how would you design a core testing strategy to regress and prevent this problem?

Options:
A. I believe this is a typical client-side state management flaw, such as the old anonymous token cached locally after successful registration not being cleared in time. My core strategy is to write a unit test for `LoginController` using the JUnit and Mockito frameworks. In the test, I will carefully construct a mock `HttpServletRequest` carrying an expired or invalid JWT in the request header. Then, I will focus on asserting that in this scenario, the interface must return a `401 Unauthorized` status code, and the response body must contain a clear error code, such as `{'error_code': 1002, 'message': 'Invalid credentials'}`, to ensure the robustness of backend defensive checks and prevent dirty data from causing downstream issues.
B. I will write a backend integration test case. This test case will directly call `RegisterService` via code to create a new user. Then, after a very short delay (e.g., within 100 milliseconds), it will immediately call `LoginService` with the same user information. Finally, it will use `Assert` to verify that the login service successfully returns the user entity and a valid JWT, ensuring the timeliness and consistency of data writes and reads under high concurrency.
C. This is clearly a frontend state management issue. I would write a unit test using Jest and React Testing Library specifically for the Redux store's update logic. The test would simulate dispatching a `registerSuccess` action, then immediately assert that the `user` and `token` states in the store have been correctly updated. I would also mock API requests to verify that subsequent axios instances carry the latest authentication token in their headers, addressing the problem at its root.
D. I would use an end-to-end testing framework like Cypress or Playwright to write automation scripts. The scripts would fully simulate the user's operational flow: visiting the registration page, filling in a randomly generated username and password, clicking register, waiting for the page to redirect to the login page, then immediately logging in with the newly registered account, and asserting whether the page successfully redirected to the user's backend. This method best replicates real user scenarios.
gold: B. I will write a backend integration test case. This test case will directly call `RegisterService` via code to create a new user. Then, after a very short delay (e.g., within 100 milliseconds), it will immediately call `LoginService` with the same user information. Finally, it will use `Assert` to verify that the login service successfully returns the user entity and a valid JWT, ensuring the timeliness and consistency of data writes and reads under high concurrency.

I (Si Jia) am preparing a presentation for new team members on "R&D Efficiency Improvement." One key point is to introduce our new approach to troubleshooting cross-service issues. Could you help me draft a speech, focusing on how this change impacts our daily development work?

Options:
A. This new change is the Grafana Loki logging system, led and introduced by Director Mingzhi Li, which is deeply integrated with our Prometheus monitoring system. The biggest impact on our daily development is that when troubleshooting issues, we can now directly use LogQL for high-performance tag queries on Grafana dashboards, such as filtering by pod or namespace. This not only allows us to view logs but also to correlate and analyze them with performance metrics. This is extremely helpful for quickly pinpointing and fixing business logic errors in our code, especially intermittent issues, and also enhances the observability of our code.
B. This change primarily refers to the unified logging platform built by Hongfang Xiong based on ELK. For our daily development, the biggest impact is on the efficiency of troubleshooting. Previously, to investigate a problem, we might have had to log into several servers. Now, when a request comes in, we can directly search in Kibana using the TraceID to see its complete logs across all links, such as the user service and archive service. This significantly speeds up our ability to locate business logic bugs in our own code and makes it easier to understand the relationships between service calls.
C. This new method refers to Hongfang Xiong's recently completed development environment based on Docker-Compose and ELK. For us, the key is to understand the architecture of this environment. The core is the `docker-compose.yml` file, which defines the startup order and network for all services. For logging, he resolved the compatibility issues between Logstash and Elasticsearch and wrote grok rules for different services to parse logs. Newcomers need to become familiar with these configurations, which is crucial for our future maintenance and expansion of this environment.
D. This new change refers to the Grafana Loki logging system led by Director Mingzhi Li. For us, the core task is to maintain the stable operation of this system. We need to learn how to configure Promtail's scrape_configs to ensure that logs from all services can be collected, and manage Loki's data sources and storage lifecycle. Oh, I need to quickly confirm something with you. I'm working on the new drug payment feature and encountered an edge case: what's the best user experience if the payment request fails after the user clicks "Pay Now" due to a server glitch? I recall we discussed a similar scenario before, but I don't have time to dig through chat logs right now. Can you help me remember what we decided back then?

Options:
A. The user should be redirected to a separate order status page displaying "Payment failed. Please check your order in the Order Center later." This solution was confirmed by Hanqiang Liang at the technical review meeting on July 5. He believes this approach better handles the asynchronous nature of payment callbacks and prevents the front-end from getting stuck.
B. A lightweight toast notification should pop up to inform the user that the payment failed, and the payment pop-up window should remain open, allowing the user to click a button to retry directly. This solution follows the interaction design principles for appointment failure scenarios previously proposed by Hao Lv and confirmed by Huilan Chen, aiming to reduce the number of steps for the user to re-operate.
C. A toast notification should first pop up, then the pop-up window should automatically close, and the system should silently retry three times in the background. This is the advanced interaction strategy finalized by Huilan Chen at the "Core Link Experience Optimization" special meeting on July 10. This solution aims to achieve imperceptible retries, minimizing active user operations. If it still fails after three attempts, the user will be notified of the order anomaly via a system message.
D. Immediately close the payment pop-up and display a modal dialog box prompting "Payment failed, please return and try again." According to the latest "UI/UX Interaction Specification V2.1" released by the project team, all transaction failure scenarios must use a strong prompt to interrupt the process, guiding users to start over and ensuring data consistency.
gold: B. A lightweight toast notification should pop up to inform the user that the payment failed, and the payment pop-up window should remain open, allowing the user to click a button to retry directly. A. Should return a string in ISO 8601 standard format (e.g., '2025-09-15T10:30:00Z'). At the technical architecture review meeting on August 15, it was decided that all new interface time formats must follow ISO 8601 to align with international standards and completely resolve timezone issues.

This is a new specification finalized by Mingzhi Li on August 20 during a special discussion on the chronic disease management module. It aims to make the data returned by the interface more readable and to clarify timezone information to prevent front-end misunderstandings. This specification has been incorporated into the latest project development manual.
D. It should return a string in `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss` format. To reduce the burden on the frontend and standardize display, Hanqiang Liang suggested in the general component library specification submitted on August 14 that the backend should directly return standard format strings in non-high-precision scenarios.

Hey, Assistant, urgent matter! The product team is really pushing for our 'Personalized Medication Reminder' feature. I just met with Lei Wang, and he suggested we package the desensitized user data and send it to our AI partner for joint modeling. He thinks this could save us a lot of R&D time. I think it's a good idea. I don't recall any regulations explicitly prohibiting this, do I? Could you please double-check for me? If there are no compliance risks, we'll prepare to move forward.

Options:
A. This proposal is generally feasible, but directly packaging and sending the data carries too much risk. We should adopt a 'data sandbox' approach, allowing partner organizations to access data and train models within our controlled environment, ensuring data never leaves our domain. This way, we can leverage external computing power while guaranteeing data security and control, which is a common collaboration model in the industry.
B. This proposal is not feasible. According to the principles established by Weihua Zhang on January 31, "The Final Report on Compliance Research in the Healthcare Industry" is the "fundamental law" for all our technical development. Providing user health data (even if de-identified) to any third-party organization carries extremely high compliance risks and severely violates the core principles of data security and privacy protection outlined in that report.
C. Can be executed. Boss Zhang explicitly stated at the AI Collaboration Special Meeting on February 10 that to accelerate technological breakthroughs, data cooperation with top research institutions that have passed security certification is permitted. As long as we use the latest differential privacy technology to perform secondary desensitization on the data and have the legal department review the cooperation agreement, we can initiate joint modeling. This move is considered a key step in promoting the intelligent upgrade of our online diagnosis and treatment system.
D. In principle, yes, but only after special approval from the Project Data Security Committee. Product Manager Lei Wang must lead the effort to prepare a detailed explanation of the data usage scope and a data anonymization plan, and sign a supplementary Data Confidentiality Agreement with the partner organization. As long as the process is compliant and approval is granted, it can be executed.

Ugh, this online consultation project is really pushing us. To make debugging and troubleshooting easier later on, I'm planning to log user inquiries and doctor replies from the "Doctor-Patient Communication" module directly to the logging platform in plain text. This would be the fastest way to pinpoint issues; we can't go digging through the database every time, that's too inefficient. I think this solution is viable, there shouldn't be any pitfalls, right?

Options:
A. Using a third-party logging platform might be too costly. Based on the feedback from previous technical review meetings, we recommend using the company's in-house ELK cluster to store these logs. This approach will not only meet the need for fast indexing but also effectively control the budget and unify the technology stack.
B. This solution involves sensitive data and requires approval from the security department. Please first draft a detailed technical proposal and submit it to Weihua Zhang, the security lead, for evaluation. He will provide the final opinion based on data de-identification and access control policies.
C. Storing in plaintext is too risky. According to the resolution from the architecture upgrade meeting chaired by Jianguo Huang on February 25, such sensitive data should be stored in the logging system after applying 'Field-Level Encryption'. AI Assistant, I have an urgent matter. For the online consultation backend, the product team is rushing to launch a new feature that allows customer service to see users' full phone numbers for identity verification. I was thinking, why make it complicated? Can't we just open a new API that returns the original phone number based on the user ID? This API is for the internal customer service backend anyway, not exposed externally. I think this is the fastest solution. Could you please double-check it for me? If it's fine, I'll schedule it for development right away.

Options:
A. This solution is feasible. During the special review meeting for the customer service system on June 15, Guoxin Pan confirmed that to improve the efficiency of customer identity verification, a dedicated interface can be created for the 'Level 1 Customer Service Supervisor' role to return the full mobile number. During development, strict role-based permission checks must be added to the backend interface to ensure that only users with this role can call it, and all call activities must be audited.
B. The solution is basically feasible. Considering it's for internal customer service backend use, this API can be developed. However, to ensure security, an IP whitelist restriction needs to be added at the API gateway layer to ensure that only IP ranges from the customer service department can access it. Additionally, detailed operator information for each call should be recorded in the interface logs.
C. In principle, it is not allowed. However, considering the special scenario of customer service verifying identity, a temporary access request can be submitted to Security Lead Mingyu Zhou. Once approved, the backend can develop a dedicated API to return unmasked data. This API must validate the approval ticket's validity with each call.
D. This solution is not feasible. According to the clear security specifications previously established by Guoxin Pan, all sensitive user information returned to the frontend must be desensitized. Phone numbers must strictly follow the "display first three, last four" format, and the original number is not allowed to be returned.
gold: D. This solution is not feasible. According to the clear security specifications previously established by Guoxin Pan, all sensitive user information returned to the frontend must be desensitized. Phone numbers must strictly follow the "display first three, last four" format, and the original number is not allowed to be returned.

Ugh, that concurrency bug in the online consultation system is acting up again. The order statuses are all messed up, and my boss is hounding me. It's giving me a huge headache. This bug is so elusive. I've come up with an idea: temporarily remove the database locks in the test environment. That should definitely make it consistently reproducible. I'm planning to do this. Can you check if there were any specific rules we discussed regarding this when we talked before? I don't want to overlook any potential pitfalls.

Options:
A. Yes, but a specific process must be followed. At the performance optimization special meeting on August 10, the Technical Committee approved setting up 'concurrent debugging mode' for the test environment. You need to apply to Huihong Fu to enable the configuration switch for this mode, which will temporarily use memory queues instead of database locks to troubleshoot timing issues and ensure data integrity for the main process.
B. This solution is not feasible. According to the rules set by Project Lead Mingzhi Li, concurrent updates related to state machines must be locked to ensure data consistency. Even in a test environment, temporarily removing the lock violates this core data security principle and carries extremely high risks.
C. Directly removing the lock is too risky. A more robust solution is to add detailed contextual logs in the code, without changing the locking logic, to record the entire process of acquiring, waiting for, and releasing the lock. Then, use high-concurrency stress testing to analyze the logs and pinpoint timing issues.
D. In principle, it's not recommended, but you can try a compromise. You can change the current pessimistic lock to an optimistic lock by adding a version number field to control concurrency. This will reduce lock conflicts, make it easier to reproduce issues, and to some extent prevent complete data corruption.
gold: B. This solution is not feasible. According to the rules set by Project Lead Mingzhi Li, concurrent updates related to state machines must be locked to ensure data consistency. Even in a test environment, temporarily removing the lock violates this core data security principle and carries extremely high risks.

query:
Assistant, this health monitoring system dashboard project is a bit urgent. I see that in the pie chart section, some labels are using leader lines, and it looks really messy. I told the front-end team to just put all the labels inside their respective slices, regardless of size. This way, development will be faster, and it will look cleaner. Can you double-check if this approach is okay?

Options:
A. This proposal is feasible. According to the minutes of the design review meeting on August 26, to achieve absolute visual style consistency, the meeting decided that all chart component labels must either be all internal or all external, and mixing internal and external labels is prohibited. Your suggestion fully complies with the 'all internal' principle.
B. Yes, but you need to pay attention to adaptation. According to the component library update instructions released by UI/UX Lead Jing Zhou on August 28, labels are placed internally by default, but when the ratio of font size to sector width is less than 15%, the system will automatically pop them out externally and add a leader line.
C. This proposal has already been adopted as the latest standard. At the 'Data Visualization Specification Upgrade' special meeting on September 2, chaired by Mengqing Ma, it was ultimately decided that all pie chart labels would be embedded to prioritize interface simplicity. For small sectors, the new solution is to display detailed information via a floating window (Tooltip) on hover, no longer using leader lines. The relevant resolutions have been updated in the Confluence document.
D. This proposal does not comply with the project's established design specifications. According to the design standards previously set by Mengqing Ma, to prevent text overlap on charts, all labels for sectors with excessively small areas must be displayed externally using leader lines. This rule is clearly exemplified in the Figma design mockups.
gold: D. This proposal does not comply with the project's established design specifications. According to the design standards previously set by Mengqing Ma, to prevent text overlap on charts, all labels for sectors with excessively small areas must be displayed externally using leader lines. When reviewing the payment callback processing logic, newly hired backend engineer Xiao Wang found a test case. The scenario simulated by this test case is: the system processes a successful payment callback, but when updating the user's assets, it finds that the user's account status is 'FROZEN'. Options:
A. According to Project Director Mingzhi Li's definition of the 'Core Transaction Atomicity Principle,' the system should enforce the ATOMIC_CONSISTENCY_GUARANTEE protocol. Since the 'FROZEN' account prevented asset updates, this constitutes a transaction failure. Therefore, the entire process must be fully rolled back, and a failure response returned upstream to prevent any risk of data inconsistency. This is the absolute bottom line for ensuring the security of system funds.
B. Based on the latest architecture review decision, when a 'FROZEN' account is detected, the DECOUPLED_ACK_POLICY strategy should be enabled. The core of this strategy is asynchronous decoupling: the system will immediately return a success acknowledgment to the upstream, then encapsulate the payment event and push it to a dedicated high-priority retry queue. Backend consumer services will periodically attempt to process it until the account status returns to normal. This solution aims to maximize the availability of the upstream payment gateway.
C. According to "System Fault Tolerance Design Specification v1.5", this type of situation should trigger TRANSACTION_SUSPENSION_POLICY. This policy requires the system to persist the current transaction state as 'pending', release database locks, and then return a specific 'PENDING_CONFIRMATION' code to the upstream. A separate patrol task will periodically scan these 'pending' transactions and reactivate them when conditions are met (e.g., account unfreeze).
D. The DECOUPLED_ACK_POLICY strategy defined in "System Policy Dictionary v2.1" should be followed. When an account is detected as 'FROZEN', this policy stipulates that the system should log the original event, skip all asset update operations, then create a high-priority ticket marked 'MANUAL_INTERVENTION_REQUIRED', and finally return a successful acknowledgment to the upstream payment gateway.

Wang, a backend engineer, is developing an interface for the "Smart IoT Health Monitoring System" to receive and process heart rate data reported by user wearables. During development, he encounters a physiologically unreasonable value, such as 500 bpm. He recalls that the "Frontend-Backend Separation Communication Protocol and Specification" issued by the project team requires specific error codes for business validation failures. In this scenario, how should he design the exception response logic for the interface?

Options:
A. It should adhere to the core principle of the "Frontend-Backend Separation Communication Protocol and Specification" V1.0, which is to maintain clear API contracts. The system must return a specific business error code, such as 'ERR_PHYSIOLOGICAL_VALUE_INVALID'. Although IoT data is involved, to ensure system maintainability and frontend logic consistency, vague responses should not be created for individual cases. This is standard practice for ensuring efficient frontend-backend collaboration and robust interfaces.
B. According to the security advisory, this anomaly should be marked as `SECURITY_SENSITIVE_VALIDATION`. To balance security and performance, the best practice is to return HTTP 200 OK, but append a `validation_status_code` field set to '1' (indicating validation failure) in the response body. This "soft failure" mode prevents interfaces from being maliciously scanned. Simultaneously, detailed exception context is asynchronously pushed to the data lake for deep threat analysis. This design is a recommended decoupled security pattern in modern microservice architectures.
C. It should follow the design principles of the "Edge Computing Security Gateway" and classify such anomalies as `SECURITY_VIOLATION_RAW_INPUT`. Upon capturing this flag, the gateway layer should immediately terminate the connection and return HTTP 403 Forbidden. This "zero-trust" and "fail-fast" strategy can effectively prevent anomalous data from flowing into backend core services, thereby achieving robust perimeter defense, and is a widely recognized IoT ingress protection solution in the industry.
D. After a validation exception is caught, the system logic checks if it's marked as `SECURITY_SENSITIVE_VALIDATION`. If it is, the API will return a vague HTTP 400 Bad Request status code without any response body, and the backend will immediately trigger a P0-level security alert to the internal monitoring system.

According to the project deployment checklist, the model is marked as `Guardian-Level`. When performing the pre-launch evaluation process, how should he implement the model interpretability analysis?

Options:
A. Follow the "`MODEL_QUALITY_ASSURANCE_POLICY`" defined in the "Model Training and Evaluation Flowchart". This policy serves as the baseline for model quality acceptance, requiring all models (including `Guardian-Level`) to calculate and record SHAP values. To ensure standardized processes and consistent quality acceptance, this foundational policy takes precedence over temporary security policies for specific scenarios.
B. The model should first be identified as having `PHI_SAFEGUARD_POLICY` enabled. According to the supplementary execution guidelines for this policy, to balance security and debugging needs, the system will initiate "agent interpretability" mode: SHAP values will be calculated in memory for a small portion (e.g., 5%) of obfuscated validation data, and these values will be destroyed immediately after analysis, without generating persistent logs. This is an advanced practice for conducting limited analysis while ensuring privacy.
C. For `Guardian-Level` models, the "`SECURE_ENCLAVE_COMPUTING_PROTOCOL`" defined by the security architecture should be activated. This protocol requires loading the model and data into a Trusted Execution Environment (TEE) for evaluation. Within this environment, SHAP values can be computed normally, but the results will not be returned directly. Instead, a signed "Model Risk Summary Report" will be generated to ensure that the original feature contributions are not leaked.
D. The model should be checked to see if it is constrained by the `PHI_SAFEGUARD_POLICY`. Since `Guardian-Level` models are forced to follow this policy, the evaluation process should skip feature-level interpretability analysis such as SHAP values, and only perform calculations of macroscopic performance metrics like AUC and Precision.

Xiao Wang, a new backend engineer, has taken on a core feature development task in the 'Chronic Disease Management Service' project. He needs to design a mechanism that can automatically generate and send follow-up appointment reminders based on key health indicators uploaded by users (e.g., blood glucose levels exceeding the normal range for a week). At the project kickoff meeting, the Product Manager emphasized that to quickly launch the product, existing implementations from mature internal company projects should be reused as much as possible. Xiao Wang also learned that the 'Real-time Online Consultation Service System' has a similar reminder function. When designing the technical solution, how should Xiao Wang plan the implementation path for this feature?

Options:
A. It should follow the company-level platform strategy and Huilan Chen's principle of experience consistency. During design, the `consistency_policy` field should be checked. If it is `UNIFIED_UX_V1`, the logic of the 'Real-time Online Diagnosis and Treatment Service System' should be directly reused. This minimizes architectural fragmentation and avoids introducing new technology stacks for individual features, which is standard practice for maintaining long-term technical health.
B. It should adopt an advanced microservices architecture. When `PROC_STRATEGY_ID` is identified as `MED_DECISION_CORE`, it should be handled using the 'Compliance Sidecar Pattern'. This means the main service continues to call the mature 'Real-time Online Diagnosis and Treatment Service System' logic, while the Sidecar container is responsible for intercepting and recording all decision logs to meet compliance audit requirements. This non-invasive design perfectly balances code reuse, rapid delivery, and compliance requirements.
C. Based on the risk classification principles emphasized by Mingzhi Li in the v2.1 specification email, the `risk_classification_id` field should be introduced. When a scenario is identified as `CLASS_IIA_MEDICAL_DEVICE`, a separate, security-hardened sandboxed instance should be created for the 'Real-time Online Diagnosis and Treatment Service System' alert module to handle the logic. This isolation mechanism is an industry best practice for ensuring the security of core medical decisions.
D. D. It should follow the v2.1 technical selection specification released by Mingzhi Li. Since this feature involves automatic medical decision-making based on physiological indicators, the processing strategy `PROC_STRATEGY_ID: MED_DECISION_CORE` must be applied. This strategy requires all core logic to be implemented in an independent, certified `MedRule-Engine-V2` rule engine.

Xiao Zhou, a new product assistant, is designing a user survey for the "Smart IoT Health Monitoring System" project, aiming to understand users' experience with the data synchronization function. He recalls that the data analysis team's guidelines emphasize using quantitative ratings for frequency-related questions to facilitate statistics. However, the target users for this survey are elderly patients with chronic diseases in partner communities. When designing the question "How often do you experience data synchronization failures?", how should Xiao Zhou set the options to meet both project requirements and company guidelines?

Options:
A. Follow the core specifications set by the data analysis team to ensure the long-term value of data assets. For frequency-related questions, uniformly adopt the `QUANT_STANDARD_L5` (Level 5 Quantification Standard) scheme, which is a 1-5 point Likert scale. Although there are cognitive challenges for specific user groups, maintaining data structure consistency is the basis for subsequent longitudinal studies and model training, and thus has a higher priority.
B. The `HYBRID_SEMANTIC_SCALE` model, designed specifically for cognitively sensitive groups, should be adopted. This model is enabled under the `POLICY_A11Y_FIRST` strategy and combines an abstract 3-point scale (1-Rarely, 2-Sometimes, 3-Frequently) with concrete emojis (e.g., frowning face, neutral face, smiling face). This design has been proven in multiple usability tests to effectively balance data analyzability with user comprehension costs.
C. Enable the `POLICY_A11Y_ADAPTIVE` adaptive policy. The system will dynamically adjust how options are presented based on the user's initial response time and click hesitation. For users who respond quickly, a standard 5-point scale will be displayed; for users who respond slowly, it will automatically switch to the two core options of "Occasionally" and "Frequently." This adheres to the personalized design principles of user experience.
D. Should follow the `POLICY_A11Y_FIRST` policy, abandon numerical scales, and directly use concrete descriptive words as options, such as: 'almost always', 'often', 'occasionally', 'almost never'.
gold: D. Should follow the `POLICY_A11Y_FIRST` policy, abandon numerical scales, and directly use concrete descriptive words as options, such as: 'almost always', 'often', 'occasionally', 'almost never'.

A. This is to adhere to the unified specification of system data interfaces. According to design principles, all list interfaces should default to the `STD_SORT_CHRONO_DESC` strategy, meaning sorting in reverse chronological order. Even for administrator views, this basic rule should be maintained to ensure the predictability of API behavior. Any special sorting requirements should be implemented through independent reporting interfaces, rather than by modifying core query interfaces.

query:
I (Huihong Fu) need to sync the "Unified Notification Gateway" design proposal with the team. Please help me draft a group message.

Options:
A. Colleagues, regarding the "Unified Notification Gateway" solution, the conclusion is as follows: To ensure the rapid delivery of the Smart IoT Health Monitoring project, V1 will adopt a simplified design. The gateway will only support routing functionality for App Push channels. Regarding message sending idempotency, this issue will be handled by the upstream business callers themselves; the gateway layer will not include this logic. Subsequent versions will iterate on other channels such as SMS and WeChat based on business development.
B. Colleagues, we are now sharing the design proposal for the "Unified Notification Gateway." This gateway aims to unify the management of various notification channels (including App Push, SMS, and WeChat). To control costs, the gateway will integrate a strategy engine to automatically select channels based on message priority or user preferences, while also retaining an interface for callers to specify channels. Additionally, to avoid duplicate notifications, the system will achieve message sending idempotence through a unique request ID. Please review this proposal.
C. Morning all! 🚀 Regarding the 'Unified Notification Gateway' mentioned by Mingzhi Li and Huilan Chen, I've put together a preliminary proposal and wanted to share my thoughts. The core idea is to create a unified entry point that encapsulates channels like App Push, SMS, and WeChat. For costly channels like SMS, the gateway will have a built-in strategy engine to automatically select the channel based on message priority and user preferences. Of course, the caller can also "force" a specific channel. Additionally, idempotency will definitely be handled; each request will come with a unique ID to ensure that even if there's a mistake, messages won't be sent repeatedly. Please let me know if you see any issues. 🤔💪
D. Morning all! 🚀 I've been thinking about the 'Unified Notification Gateway' solution. To get it online quickly, let's start with a lightweight V1. The gateway will primarily handle routing, and we'll integrate the App Push channel first. SMS, WeChat, and other channels can wait for V2. Also, regarding idempotency, considering the gateway's pure routing function, I suggest that each business caller be responsible for this logic themselves. They can generate a unique ID before passing parameters, and the gateway won't handle duplicate processing, keeping it lightweight. This way, we can deliver results faster! What do you all think? 💪🎉
